title: Surendra Kumar v. State of U.P.
coram: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi, J.; Vivek Kumar Singh, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; fresh representation to be decided under Supply Code cl. 6.1.
headnote: On a writ challenging a CGRF direction to deposit Rs 63,360 after a 1 kW Saubhagya connection was billed at 2 kW, the Allahabad High Court, without examining the Forum order or the load/billing dispute, disposed of the petition by consent and directed the consumer to file a fresh representation to be considered strictly under clause 6.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Surendra Kumar received a 1 kW Saubhagya connection from Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited on 6 September 2019. The department then billed him for 2 kW from 31 October 2019. He complained to the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum, Vindhyachal Mandal, Mirzapur (Complaint No. 659 of 2020). On 5 September 2022 the Forum directed him to deposit Rs 63,360. A later representation dated 29 November 2022 to the licensee remained pending. He sought quashing of the Forum order and a correct 1 kW bill.

holding_units.holding: With consent, the writ challenging a CGRF direction to deposit Rs 63,360 on a 1 kW Saubhagya connection billed at 2 kW was disposed of without examining the Forum order. The consumer was to file a fresh representation within three weeks for consideration strictly under clause 6.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the licensee remaining free to proceed in accordance with law.
holding_units.flag: Order cites 'section 6.1' of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 without quoting its text; clause number taken as stated.

principle_tags.application: Licensee counsel accepted that a pending representation would be dealt with strictly under clause 6.1. The Court disposed of the writ on that concession, directing a fresh representation to be considered under the same clause, without construing 6.1 or deciding the CGRF order.

not_decided.point: Validity of the CGRF order dated 05.09.2022 directing deposit of Rs 63,360
Whether billing a 1 kW Saubhagya connection at 2 kW was lawful
Whether a correct 1 kW bill must issue
